title: ～のが上手だ — being good at doing something
summary: Verb (dictionary form) + のが上手です means ‘is good at ～ing’. の makes the verb a noun phrase and 上手 is a な-adjective. It is a natural way to praise a skill.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形＋のが上手だ
patterns.gloss: dictionary form + のが上手だ (歌うのが上手)
noun + が上手だ (料理が上手)

body.p: Dictionary form + の + が上手です: 料理をするのが上手です. The skill is marked with が.
Saying someone is 上手 is a compliment, so you can use it for others. About yourself, Japanese people usually stay modest and avoid saying 上手 directly.
Shorter versions exist: 料理が上手です (good at cooking). The opposite is のが下手です. Another common pair is のが好きです (like ～ing).

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）は料理（りょうり）をするのが上手（じょうず）です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa ryōri o suru no ga jōzu desu.

examples.ja: 姉（あね）は歌（うた）うのが上手（じょうず）です。
examples.romaji: Ane wa utau no ga jōzu desu.
examples.tr: My older sister is good at singing.
examples.note: 姉 is your own older sister (said to others).

examples.ja: 友（とも）だちは字（じ）を書（か）くのが上手（じょうず）です。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi wa ji o kaku no ga jōzu desu.
examples.tr: My friend is good at writing characters.
examples.note: 字を書く means writing characters / handwriting.

pitfalls: Use が, not を, before 上手: 歌うのが上手です.
Don't use 上手です to praise yourself; it sounds boastful. It is mainly for others.
